mainTopic: Washing hands for bread (a cloth, being fed, feeding), and keeping meat and cheese apart (one cloth, two guests at one table)
overview: The גמרא finishes the story of רב eating with a cloth on his hands. He explains that he did wash, but he is delicate. רבי זירא then challenges רבי אמי and רבי אסי for eating with old wineskins on their hands instead of washing. The גמרא answers that a cloth is allowed for כהנים eating תרומה, and these two were כהנים. Next the גמרא asks two questions: does someone who is fed by another person need to wash, and does the one feeding him need to wash? Several proofs are brought and pushed away, and the final הלכה is that the eater washes and the feeder does not. A new משנה then allows meat and cheese in one cloth if they don't touch. אביי explains that cold foods that touch still need rinsing. שמואל limits the משנה's ruling on two guests eating meat and cheese at one table to guests who are strangers. Finally, רב יימר asks אביי about two brothers who don't share food, and he challenges אביי's answer; that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמואל asks רב: Do we really act this way?
steps.stepSummary: שמואל finishes his challenge to רב, who was eating bread with a cloth on his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do we act like this?
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes שמואל's question to רב, which started just before this. He saw רב eating bread while holding it with a cloth, and he asks if that is a proper way to act.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל thinks רב used the cloth to avoid washing his hands. So he is really challenging רב: is it okay to skip נטילת ידים just by covering your hands?

keyTerms.meaning: Do we act like this? A short way of questioning whether something is proper

phrases.english: Do we act like this?
phrases.notes: שמואל is asking רב, who was holding his bread with a cloth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the question that began just before this text.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's behavior of eating bread with his hands covered by a cloth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It looks like רב is using a cloth to get out of washing his hands, which should not be allowed.

steps.title: רב answers: I am delicate
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that he did wash. He uses the cloth only because he is sensitive about touching food.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I am delicate.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers שמואל: the cloth is not a replacement for washing. He is just a delicate person who does not like touching food with his bare hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge only works if רב skipped washing. רב says he did wash, so the cloth was just a personal preference and not a way around the הלכה.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'my mind is short on me', meaning I am delicate or squeamish

phrases.english: He said to him:
I am delicate.
phrases.notes: Literally 'my mind is short on me.' רב means he washed, but he does not like touching food with bare hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers שמואל's challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the facts: the cloth was not used in place of washing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב used the cloth so he would not have to wash.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב washed, and the cloth was only because he is delicate.
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי זירא will use this exact answer in the next step to challenge רבי אמי and רבי אסי.

steps.title: רבי זירא challenges רבי אמי and רבי אסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא sees רבי אמי and רבי אסי eating with old wineskins on their hands instead of washing, and challenges them based on the רב and שמואל story.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי זירא went up to ארץ ישראל, he found רבי אמי and רבי אסי eating with worn-out wineskins on their hands. He said: Could two great men like you make a mistake about the story of רב and שמואל? רב said 'I am delicate', which means he did wash!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא sees two great sages eating bread while covering their hands with old wineskins and not washing. He asks how they could misunderstand the story of רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא thinks they learned from רב that a covering can replace washing. But רב only used a cloth after washing ('I am delicate'), so the story does not support them.

keyTerms.meaning: Went up, here meaning moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: When Rabbi Zeira went up,
phrases.notes: He moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he found Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi
eating with worn-out wineskins.
phrases.notes: They wrapped their hands in old leather so they would not touch the bread, instead of washing.

phrases.english: He said: Two great men like you,
should make a mistake about the case of Rav and Shmuel?
But he said, 'I am delicate'!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּרֵי גַּבְרֵי רַבְרְבֵי כְּוָותַיְיכוּ, לִיטְעוֹ בִּדְרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רב's answer from step 2 to challenge רבי אמי and רבי אסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי and רבי אסי eating with covered hands without washing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only source for using a covering is the story of רב, and רב had washed first. So nothing allows a covering instead of washing.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא is not saying covering your hands is forbidden. He is saying a covering cannot replace washing, because רב washed too.

steps.title: A cloth is allowed for כהנים who eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי זירא forgot שמואל's rule: a cloth is allowed for people eating תרומה, and רבי אמי and רבי אסי were כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He forgot what רב תחליפא בר אבימי said in the name of שמואל: They allowed a cloth for people who eat תרומה, but they did not allow a cloth for people who eat טהרות. And רבי אמי and רבי אסי were כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אמי and רבי אסי. רבי זירא forgot a rule of שמואל that lets כהנים eating תרומה use a cloth instead of washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים are very careful about keeping תרומה pure, so they can be trusted not to touch the bread through the cloth. People who just try to eat regular food in purity (טהרות) are not as careful, so they must wash. Since רבי אמי and רבי אסי were כהנים, they were allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: It slipped his mind; he forgot
A cloth used to cover the hands
Those who eat תרומה, meaning כהנים
People who are careful to eat their regular food in purity
Priests, who are allowed to eat תרומה

phrases.english: It slipped his mind, this

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: that Rav Tachlifa bar Avimi said in the name of Shmuel:
They allowed a cloth for those who eat terumah,
but they did not allow a cloth for those who eat in purity,
phrases.notes: These are people who are not כהנים but try to eat their everyday food in purity.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי אַסִּי כֹּהֲנִים הֲווֹ.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi were kohanim.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִשְׁתְּמִיטְתֵּיהּ הָא דְּאָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי זירא's challenge from step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a separate source that gives a special rule for כהנים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nobody may use a covering in place of washing, because רב only used one after washing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Covering the hands works for כהנים eating תרומה, because they are extra careful. It does not work for others.
steps.whatToRemember: A cloth instead of washing works for כהנים eating תרומה, not for ordinary people who eat טהרות. רבי אמי and רבי אסי were כהנים, so they did nothing wrong.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the need to wash depends on how careful the eater will be not to touch the food.

steps.title: Does someone who is fed by another person need to wash?
steps.stepSummary: A new question: if someone else puts food into your mouth and you never touch it, do you need נטילת ידים?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: someone who eats because another person feeds him, does he need נטילת ידים or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. If the eater never touches the food because someone else feeds him, must he still wash his hands?
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just learned that covering the hands can sometimes replace washing because the hands do not touch the food. Here the hands do not touch the food at all, so maybe no washing is needed. Or maybe the חכמים require everyone who eats bread to wash, no matter what.

keyTerms.meaning: One who eats because someone else feeds him
Washing the hands before eating bread

phrases.english: A question was asked:
One who eats because someone feeds him,
does he need to wash his hands or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the idea that washing is about the hands touching food.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether נטילת ידים is needed when the eater's hands never touch the food because he is fed by someone else.

steps.title: Proof attempt from רב הונא בר סחורה feeding רב המנונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a story where רב הונא בר סחורה put meat into רב המנונא's mouth and said he would not do this for anyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב הונא בר סחורה was standing before רב המנונא. He put a piece of meat into his mouth, and he ate it. He said to him: If you were not רב המנונא, I would not feed you.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to try to answer the question. It is setting up the next move, where the גמרא will figure out what this story proves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא בר סחורה fed רב המנונא directly. His comment, 'I would not feed you if you were not רב המנונא', hints that only someone as careful as רב המנונא could be fed this way, perhaps even without having washed. The next step tries to read the story that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Put the food into his mouth

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר סְחוֹרָה הֲוָה קָאֵי
phrases.english: that Rav Huna bar Sechora was standing
before Rav Hamnuna,
he put a piece of meat into his mouth, and he ate.
phrases.notes: רב המנונא did not touch the food at all; it went straight into his mouth.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי לָאו דְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא אַתְּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: If you were not Rav Hamnuna,
I would not feed you.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּרַב הוּנָא בַּר סְחוֹרָה הֲוָה קָאֵי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from step 5 using a real story.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one who is fed by another needs נטילת ידים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב הונא בר סחורה feeding רב המנונא and saying he would not do it for anyone else

steps.title: Trying to prove from רב המנונא that no washing is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב המנונא was allowed to be fed without washing because he was careful not to touch the food.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why was this allowed? Isn't it because רב המנונא was careful and did not touch the food?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is drawing the lesson it wants from the story in Step 6. It suggests that רב המנונא did not wash, and that this was fine because he never touched the food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If this reading is right, it answers the question from Step 5: a person who is fed by someone else does not need נטילת ידים. The proof depends on assuming that רב המנונא did not wash his hands.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He means: why was רב המנונא allowed to be fed this way, in the story from just before?

phrases.english: Is it not because he was careful and did not touch it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic lesson from the story in Step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That someone fed by another, who does not touch the food, does not need נטילת ידים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב הונא בר סחורה feeding meat to רב המנונא.

steps.title: Maybe רב המנונא washed anyway
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: רב המנונא was quick and had already washed his hands before eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. He was quick and went ahead and washed his hands at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from Step 7. It says we can't know that רב המנונא ate without washing. Maybe he washed first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from Step 7 only works if רב המנונא never washed. If he did wash, the story tells us nothing about someone who did not wash. So this proof fails; the final ruling on the question from Step 5 comes in Step 18.

keyTerms.meaning: Quick and eager to do a מצוה
Went ahead and did it early

phrases.english: No, for he was quick and went ahead
and washed his hands at the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof suggested in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the story. It does not decide the question either way.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed רב המנונא did not wash, but he may have washed beforehand.

steps.title: A new proof from רב's rule about feeding a waiter
steps.stepSummary: רב said you may not put bread into a שמש's mouth unless you know he washed. The same statement also deals with which ברכות the שמש says, where רבי יוחנן disagrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי זירא said in the name of רב: A person may not put a slice of bread into a waiter's mouth unless he knows that the waiter washed his hands. The waiter makes a ברכה on every cup, but not on every slice of bread. רבי יוחנן says: he makes a ברכה on every slice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source to answer the question from Step 5. רב says even a waiter who is being fed by someone else needs to have washed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The waiter does not touch the bread, because it is put straight into his mouth. Still, רב says he needs washed hands. That seems to show that being fed by another person still requires נטילת ידים. The part about ברכות is a side detail that comes with the same quote.

keyTerms.meaning: A waiter or attendant serving at a meal
A slice or piece of bread

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for רבי זירא said that רב said:
A person may not put a slice of bread
into the mouth of a waiter,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יוֹדֵעַ בּוֹ שֶׁנָּטַל יָדָיו.
phrases.english: unless he knows about him that he washed his hands.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַשַּׁמָּשׁ מְבָרֵךְ עַל כׇּל כּוֹס וָכוֹס,
phrases.english: And the waiter makes a ברכה on each and every cup,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ מְבָרֵךְ עַל כׇּל פְּרוּסָה וּפְרוּסָה.
phrases.english: but he does not make a ברכה on each and every slice.
And רבי יוחנן says:
He makes a ברכה on each and every slice.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, a new proof is brought for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: That someone fed by another still needs נטילת ידים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's rule that a waiter may only be fed if he is known to have washed.

steps.title: רב פפא settles רב and רבי יוחנן on the waiter's ברכות
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says there is no real argument between רב and רבי יוחנן. One case has an important person at the meal and the other does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The disagreement between רב and רבי יוחנן is not a problem. One case is where there is an important person at the meal, and the other is where there is no important person.
steps.whatsHappening: Before pushing the main proof, רב פפא clears up the side issue about ברכות. He shows that רב and רבי יוחנן are talking about different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב, who says one ברכה is enough, is talking about a meal with an important person. רבי יוחנן, who says a ברכה on every slice, is talking about a meal without one. The word בשלמא ("granted") tells us רב פפא is setting this aside so he can return to the main point.

keyTerms.meaning: An important person at the meal

phrases.english: רב פפא said: Granted,
between רב and רבי יוחנן there is no problem:
this one is where there is an important person,
phrases.notes: "This one" is רב, who said the waiter does not need a ברכה on every slice.

phrases.english: that one is where there is no important person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַב וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the side argument about ברכות inside the source quoted in Step 9.
steps.confusionAlert: This ברכה discussion is only a side point. The real question is still whether a person who is fed needs to wash, and that comes back in the next step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different cases: each opinion is talking about a different kind of meal.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב and רבי יוחנן seem to argue about whether the waiter needs a ברכה on every slice.
steps.terutzMaskana: They do not argue. With an important person, one ברכה is enough. Without one, a ברכה is needed on every slice.

steps.title: Back to the proof: רב requires the waiter to wash
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא goes back to the main point: either way, רב said the waiter must have washed, so being fed seems to require washing.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, רב does say: unless he knows that the waiter washed his hands!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא returns from the side issue and presses the proof from Step 9. רב clearly said the waiter must have washed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: However we settle the ברכות, רב's first rule still stands. A waiter being fed by someone else needs washed hands. This seems to answer the question from Step 5: yes, washing is needed.

phrases.english: In any case, he does say:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁנָּטַל יָדָיו!
phrases.english: unless he knows that he washed his hands!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comes back from the side issue in Step 10 to the main proof from Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That a person fed by someone else needs נטילת ידים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's words: unless he knows that the waiter washed his hands.

steps.title: A waiter is different because he is busy
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: a waiter is busy with his work and might touch the food by accident, so he must wash. That does not prove the rule for everyone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: A waiter is different, because he is busy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רב's rule. The waiter is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A waiter is rushing around serving, so he might grab or touch the food without thinking. That is why he must wash. A person who can sit calmly and be careful not to touch might not need to, so this proof fails. The final ruling on the question from Step 5 comes in Step 18.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs were rejected. רב המנונא may have washed first, and a waiter is a special case because he is busy. The final ruling about someone who is fed comes in Step 18: he must wash.

phrases.english: A waiter is different, for he is busy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof pressed in Step 11.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's rule about a waiter comes from a special worry, the risk of touching by accident. It is not a general rule for everyone who is fed.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the waiter only. It does not decide the question about an ordinary person being fed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The waiter's case is special because he is busy and may touch the food, so it cannot teach the rule for someone who is careful.

steps.title: Do not give bread to the waiter, and never feed an unwashed waiter
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a guest should not hand a slice of bread to the שמש, in case something goes wrong at the meal. It also teaches that you may not put bread into the mouth of a שמש who has not washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A person should not give a slice of bread to the waiter, whether the cup is in the waiter's hand or in the host's hand, in case something goes wrong at the meal. And if the waiter has not washed his hands, it is forbidden to put a slice of bread into his mouth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא with two rules about the שמש at a meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule is about keeping the meal running smoothly: handing food to the waiter could lead to a mishap. The second rule matches what רב said in step 9: an unwashed waiter may not be fed bread. This leads straight into the next question about the one doing the feeding.

keyTerms.meaning: A slice or piece of bread
The waiter or attendant serving the meal
The host, the owner of the house

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A person should not give a slice to the waiter,
whether the cup is in his hand
phrases.notes: "His hand" here means the waiter's hand.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁהַכּוֹס בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: or the cup is in the hand of the host,
lest something go wrong at the meal.
And a waiter who did not wash his hands:
it is forbidden to put a slice into his mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that states as a ruling what רב said about the waiter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Don't hand bread to the waiter during the meal; don't put bread into the mouth of an unwashed waiter.

steps.title: Does someone who feeds another need to wash?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a person who feeds someone else must do נטילת ידים, or not, since he himself isn't eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: Does a person who feeds someone else need to wash his hands, or does he not need to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the person doing the feeding, not the one eating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we discussed the one being fed. Now the focus is on the feeder: his hands touch the bread, but he is not eating it. So it is unclear whether נטילת ידים applies to him.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked: the גמרא raises an open question
Ritual washing of the hands before bread

phrases.english: They asked:
One who feeds, does he need washing of hands,
or does he not need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the one being fed to the one who feeds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a person who feeds another, but does not eat, must wash his hands.

steps.title: Proof from שמאי הזקן feeding with two hands
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a woman may rinse one hand to give bread to her small son. שמאי הזקן didn't want to feed even with one washed hand, and the חכמים required him to feed with both hands. This seems to show that a feeder must wash.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, from what the school of מנשה taught: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: A woman may rinse one hand in water and give bread to her young son. They said about שמאי הזקן that he did not want to feed with even one hand, and the חכמים decreed that he must feed with both his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with a ברייתא about feeding children on יום כיפור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום כיפור washing is normally forbidden, yet the woman may rinse a hand just to feed her child. שמאי was even made to wash both hands to feed. If the feeder had no need to wash, why allow, and even require, washing on יום כיפור? So it looks like a feeder must wash.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for the school of Menashe taught:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה מְדִיחָה אֶת יָדָהּ אַחַת בַּמַּיִם,
phrases.english: A woman may rinse one of her hands in water,
phrases.notes: This is talking about יום כיפור, when washing is normally not allowed.

phrases.english: and give bread to her young son.
They said about Shammai the Elder
that he did not want to feed even with one hand,
phrases.notes: He didn't want to wash even one hand on יום כיפור, so he wouldn't feed at all.

phrases.english: and they decreed on him that he must feed with both his hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a source to answer the question of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That one who feeds another must wash his hands.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of the school of מנשה: washing hands to feed children is allowed, even required, on יום כיפור.

steps.title: אביי: that washing was because of שיבתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the proof: the washing on יום כיפור was not because of feeding. It was to remove שיבתא, a harmful spirit on hands not washed in the morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: There, the washing is because of שיבתא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the proof from שמאי and gives a different reason for the washing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The washing in that ברייתא was a morning washing to get rid of שיבתא, not a washing for bread. So it does not show that a feeder needs נטילת ידים. Someone who already washed in the morning might not need to wash again to feed.

keyTerms.meaning: A harmful spirit that rests on hands not washed in the morning

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up two different washings: the morning washing to remove שיבתא, and נטילת ידים before bread. אביי says the case of שמאי was the first kind.
steps.whatToRemember: The proof from שמאי הזקן fails because that washing was for שיבתא, not for the food. The next steps settle whether a feeder must wash.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
There it is because of Shivta.
phrases.notes: שיבתא is a harmful spirit that rests on hands that were not washed in the morning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question of step 14 is settled later, in steps 17-18.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The washing there was for removing שיבתא in the morning, not for feeding bread.

steps.title: שמואל is hit for feeding without washing, and his father defends him
steps.stepSummary: A story: שמואל's teacher hit him for feeding the teacher's son without washing. שמואל's father says the teacher was wrong. A feeder does not need to wash.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: שמואל's father found שמואל crying. He asked him: Why are you crying? Because my teacher hit me. Why? Because he said to me: You are feeding my son and you did not wash your hands. And why didn't you wash? He said: He is the one eating, and I should wash?! His father said: Isn't it enough that your teacher didn't learn the הלכה? He hits you too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story to answer the question from step 14: does someone who feeds another person have to wash his hands?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Young שמואל did not wash because he was not the one eating. His father, a great sage, agrees with him and says the teacher simply did not know the הלכה. This supports the view that a feeder does not need to wash.

keyTerms.meaning: You are feeding (from the root ספי, to feed someone)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
that Shmuel's father found Shmuel
crying.
He said to him: Why are you crying?
Because my teacher hit me.
Why? Because he said to me:
You are feeding my son
and you did not wash your hands.
And why did you not wash?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הוּא אָכֵיל וַאֲנָא מָשֵׁינָא?!
phrases.english: He said to him: He is eating, and I should wash?!
phrases.notes: "He" means the teacher's son, the one who was actually eating.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לָא מִיסָּתְיֵיהּ דְּלָא גְּמִיר,
phrases.english: He said to him: Isn't it enough for him that he did not learn,
that he also hits!

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דַּאֲבוּהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לִשְׁמוּאֵל דְּקָא בָכֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 15 was pushed away in step 16, a new proof is brought for the question from step 14.
steps.raayaObject: Whether one who feeds another must wash his hands
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of שמואל and his father, who says the teacher did not know the הלכה

steps.title: The final הלכה: the eater washes, the feeder does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that a person who is fed by someone else must wash, but the person feeding him does not need to wash.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: One who eats by being fed by someone else needs to wash his hands. One who feeds does not need to wash his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a clear ruling that answers both questions: the one from step 5 about the person being fed, and the one from step 14 about the person feeding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing depends on who is eating, not on who touches the food. So the eater must wash even though his hands never touch the bread. The feeder, who only touches the food but does not eat, is free from washing.

keyTerms.meaning: One who eats because someone else feeds him
Ritual washing of the hands before eating bread

steps.whatToRemember: The eater washes, even if someone else feeds him. The feeder does not wash.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think washing is only for the one who touches the food. Here the one who touches (the feeder) does not wash, and the one who doesn't touch (the eater) does.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
one who eats by means of a feeder
needs washing of the hands;
one who feeds does not need washing of the hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the support from the story into a final ruling, and also decides the earlier question from step 5 about the one who is fed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One who is fed must wash. One who feeds does not.

steps.title: New משנה: meat and cheese in one cloth, and two guests at one table
steps.stepSummary: A person may tie meat and cheese in one cloth as long as they don't touch. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says two guests may eat at one table, one eating meat and one eating cheese.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A person may tie meat and cheese in one cloth, as long as they do not touch each other. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Two guests may eat at one table, this one meat and that one cheese, and we are not worried.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two rules about keeping meat and cheese near each other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first rule allows meat and cheese to share one cloth, but only if they don't touch. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows two guests to eat meat and cheese at the same table, and is not worried that one will eat from the other's food.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
A person may tie up meat and cheese
in one cloth,

phrases.aramaic: וּבִלְבַד שֶׁלֹּא יְהוּ נוֹגְעִין זֶה בָּזֶה.
phrases.english: as long as they do not touch each other.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַכְסְנָאִין אוֹכְלִין עַל שֻׁלְחָן אֶחָד,
phrases.english: Two guests may eat at one table,
this one meat and that one cheese,
and they are not concerned.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ צוֹרֵר אָדָם בָּשָׂר וּגְבִינָה בְּמִטְפַּחַת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic begins with a new משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Meat and cheese may share one cloth if they don't touch. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, two guests may eat meat and cheese at one table.

steps.title: Why should touching matter if both foods are cold?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה forbids the meat and cheese from touching. Cold foods don't pass taste into each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And if they do touch each other, what of it? It is cold with cold!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the condition in the משנה that the meat and cheese must not touch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taste passes between foods through heat. When both foods are cold, nothing goes from one into the other. So why should the משנה care if they touch?

keyTerms.meaning: What of it? What difference does it make?

phrases.english: GEMARA: And if they touch each other,
what of it?
It is cold with cold!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי נוֹגֵעַ זֶה בָּזֶה, מַאי הָוֵי? צוֹנֵן בְּצוֹנֵן הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the first rule of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's condition that the meat and cheese must not touch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cold foods don't absorb from each other, so touching should cause no problem.

steps.title: אביי: cold foods still need rinsing if they touch
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that cold foods that touched don't need peeling, but they do need rinsing. That is why the משנה says they should not touch.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Granted that they don't need peeling. But don't they need rinsing?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains why touching still matters for cold meat and cheese.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since nothing soaks in when foods are cold, there is no need to cut off the spot where they touched. But some of the cheese may stick to the meat on the outside, so the meat has to be rinsed. To avoid someone eating it without rinsing, the משנה says they should not touch at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Peeling, cutting off a thin layer

steps.whatToRemember: Cold meat and cheese that touch don't need peeling, but they do need rinsing.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Granted that it does not need peeling,
phrases.notes: Peeling means cutting away a thin layer where they touched. For cold foods that isn't needed.

phrases.english: doesn't it need rinsing?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נְהִי דִּקְלִיפָה לָא בָּעֵי, הַדָּחָה מִי לָא בָּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Agrees there is no absorption, but points to a smaller need (rinsing) that still makes touching a concern
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cold foods that touch cause no problem at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: Cold foods that touch need rinsing, so the משנה forbids them from touching.

steps.title: שמואל limits the two-guests rule to strangers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling about two guests. שמואל says it only applies when they do not know each other. If they know each other, it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל said that two guests may eat at one table. רב חנן בר אמי said in the name of שמואל: this was only taught when the guests do not know each other. If they know each other, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה again and adds שמואל's limit on it: the leniency only works for strangers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry with meat and cheese at one table is that one person will take some of the other's food. Strangers will not share, so there is no worry. People who know each other might share, so they may not eat that way.

keyTerms.meaning: Guests or travelers staying away from home
'They only taught this when...' This limits a rule to a narrower case.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the key practical limit. The leniency of eating at one table depends on whether the two people would share food.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַכְסְנָאִין אוֹכְלִין עַל שׁוּלְחָן וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: Two guests may eat at one table, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the line from the משנה we saw in step 19: one guest eats meat and the other eats cheese.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר אַמֵּי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rav Chanan bar Ami said in the name of Shmuel:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין זֶה אֶת זֶה,
phrases.english: They only taught this when they do not know each other,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מַכִּירִין זֶה אֶת זֶה – אָסוּר.
phrases.english: but if they know each other, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא שֶׁאֵין מַכִּירִין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first half of the משנה (step 21) to the second half, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two guests may eat meat and cheese at one table only if they do not know each other.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל: strangers from north and south
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of two guests from opposite directions, one with meat and one with cheese. They may eat at one table. It was only forbidden in a 'one parcel' situation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, two guests stayed at one inn. One came from the north and one from the south. One brought his meat and one brought his cheese. They may eat at one table, one meat and one cheese, and they need not worry. The Sages only forbade it with 'one parcel.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports שמואל. The guests in it are clearly strangers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes guests who came from opposite ends of the land, so they obviously do not know each other. That fits שמואל's limit. The last line, 'only with one parcel,' sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: One parcel or bundle of food

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a ברייתא:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Two guests who stayed at one inn,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה בָּא מִן הַצָּפוֹן וְזֶה בָּא מִן הַדָּרוֹם,
phrases.english: this one came from the north and that one came from the south,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה בָּא בַּחֲתִיכָתוֹ וְזֶה בָּא בִּגְבִינָתוֹ,
phrases.english: this one came with his piece of meat and that one came with his cheese,
they may eat at one table,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה בָּשָׂר וְזֶה גְּבִינָה, וְאֵין חוֹשְׁשִׁין.
phrases.english: this one meat and that one cheese, and they need not worry.
And they only forbade it with one parcel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings support for שמואל's limit from step 22.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that only strangers may eat meat and cheese at one table
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא describing guests from north and south, which means strangers

steps.title: Why would the ברייתא need to forbid one parcel?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא could mean a real single parcel. That would be obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: One parcel? Could you really think that is what it means?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's last line. If both people eat from the very same bundle, of course it is forbidden, so why say it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat and cheese mixed in one parcel is plainly forbidden. A ברייתא does not need to teach something so obvious. So 'one parcel' must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Could it enter your mind?' The גמרא uses this to reject a reading as impossible.

phrases.english: One parcel? Could that enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording at the end of the ברייתא quoted in step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'they only forbade it with one parcel'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Eating meat and cheese from the same bundle is obviously forbidden, so the ברייתא would not need to say it.

steps.title: It means 'like one parcel': people who would share
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means a situation that is like one parcel, where the two people know each other and would share.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means something like one parcel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא means people who are close enough that it is as if their food were one bundle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When two people know each other, neither minds if the other takes some food. So their two meals are treated almost like one shared parcel. This brings the ברייתא back in line with שמואל.
steps.whatToRemember: Strangers may eat meat and cheese at one table. People who know each other may not, because their food is treated 'like one parcel.'

phrases.english: Rather, something like one parcel.
phrases.notes: He means people who know each other and would share, so it is almost as if their food were one bundle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 24.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'One parcel' meant food really mixed in one bundle, which would be too obvious to teach.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'One parcel' means people who know each other, whose food is treated as if shared.

steps.title: What about two brothers who are strict with each other?
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר בר שלמיא asks אביי about two brothers who are careful not to let each other eat their food. May they eat meat and cheese at one table?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר בר שלמיא said to אביי: two brothers who are strict with each other, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. It tests the rule about people who know each other in an unusual case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Brothers know each other well, which points to forbidden. But these brothers are strict about not sharing, which is the reason strangers are allowed. The question is which factor decides.

keyTerms.meaning: Strict, particular; they mind if the other takes their food

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יֵימַר בַּר שֶׁלֶמְיָא לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Yeimar bar Shelemya said to Abaye:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, וּמַקְפִּידִין זֶה עַל זֶה, מַהוּ?
phrases.english: Two brothers who are strict with each other, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, וּמַקְפִּידִין זֶה עַל זֶה, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule from steps 22-25 to a new borderline case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether brothers who know each other but refuse to share are treated like strangers, so they may eat at one table, or like acquaintances, so they may not.

steps.title: אביי answers with the case of ביתוס's cakes
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the brothers may not eat meat and cheese at one table. He compares it to ביתוס's cakes: people would say 'all such cakes are forbidden, and only ביתוס's are allowed?!'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: People will say, 'All the fancy cakes are forbidden, but ביתוס's fancy cakes are allowed?!'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the question from step 26 by saying no. Even careful brothers may not eat meat and cheese at one table, just as the חכמים did not allow ביתוס his fancy cakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The brothers' carefulness may really protect them, but the rule is a general one. If we allowed them, it would look like a private exception, and people would get confused about the rule. So, as with ביתוס, no special exceptions are made.

keyTerms.meaning: Fancy decorated cakes, which the חכמים forbade baking for פסח
A person (ביתוס בן זונין) who wanted permission to bake these cakes in a safe way and was refused
'People will say.' This is the worry that others will misunderstand an exception

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key principle: a general rule of the חכמים usually does not bend for individuals, even when the reason for the rule does not apply to them.

phrases.english: He said to him: They will say,
phrases.notes: אביי is answering רב יימר בר שלמיא's question about the two brothers.

phrases.english: 'All the decorated cakes are forbidden,'
phrases.notes: These are fancy cakes the חכמים forbade for פסח, since making them takes so long that the dough might become חמץ.

phrases.english: 'but the decorated cakes of Baitos are permitted?!'

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: יאמרו כל הסריקין אסורין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question asked in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Forbidden. Like ביתוס's cakes, no private exception is made to a general rule, so that people will not be confused.

steps.title: רב יימר challenges: what about the person with only one shirt?
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר challenges אביי's reasoning. רבי יוחנן allowed a person with only one shirt to wash it on חול המועד, even though washing is normally forbidden then. Shouldn't people say 'everyone is forbidden but he is allowed?!' The challenge continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to your reasoning, what about what רבי אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: someone who has only one shirt may wash it on חול המועד? There too, people will say:
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר בר שלמיא pushes back on אביי's answer. He brings a case where the חכמים clearly did allow an individual exception. The sentence is cut off here and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said a general rule cannot have private exceptions, because of what people will say. But laundering on חול המועד is generally forbidden, and רבי יוחנן still allowed the man with one shirt. So the worry 'people will say' does not always stop an exception, and אביי's reasoning seems too strong.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And according to your reasoning.' This turns someone's own logic against them
The middle days of פסח or סוכות, when laundering is normally forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: רב יימר is not arguing about laundering. He uses the laundering case only to show that the חכמים sometimes do allow an individual exception.

phrases.english: But according to your reasoning,
what about that which Rabbi Asi said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא חָלוּק אֶחָד
phrases.english: one who has only one shirt
is permitted to launder it on the intermediate days of a Festival.
People will say:
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going on the next amud, where we hear what people would say.

steps.triggerLanguage: ולטעמיך, הא דאמר רבי אסי אמר רבי יוחנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning אביי used in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's principle that no private exception is allowed because 'people will say' it is unfair or confusing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן allowed the man with one shirt to launder on חול המועד, an individual exception to a general ban. So the 'people will say' worry does not always block exceptions.
